candidates.lead: From £8 bratwursts to £11 Yorkshire pudding wraps, why is the cost of the markets rising year on year?
candidates.evidence_text: Mention Christmas markets these days and the conversation often turns to rising prices – from £8 bratwursts, £11 Yorkshire pudding wraps and even £5 for a few marshmallow sticks But what do the people behind the stalls think? Traders at Manchester's Christmas markets told the BBC they were feeling the pressure of increasing bills for staff, ingredients and energy, with some saying they were making less money despite charging more One trader said it costs at least £4,000 a day to run each her four stalls, while another has cut prices to keep customers coming back Nils Borstel, 25, helps run Bratwurst King, a family business which has operated at the markets since 1999 He said a sausage that previously cost £3.50 now sold for £8, with much of the increase taking place over the past five or six years

It is understood the Tories agreed to pay a £1,000 fee for use of the image - and contributed an unknown sum to Chow's legal fees The Conservatives had distributed water bottles with the image on them - accusing Burnham of being a "bottler" Chow posted on Facebook: "The Conservative Party have settled after their recent indiscretion of using my image without my permission." He added: "Maybe ask first… admittedly I would have said no, but it would have been a damn sight cheaper for the Tory Party if they just hired any illustrator to do their take on a cartoon of Burnham… hopefully this a lesson learned. candidates.title: Dismay as Leigh veterans' handmade war memorial stolen
candidates.summary: Handmade wooden silhouettes of soldiers have been taken from a roundabout in Leigh
candidates.reason: Dedupe: live item has no exact/history repeat; accepted for editorial selection. | Selection: Protected item selected before size limits.

candidates.lead: Handmade wooden silhouettes of soldiers have been taken from a roundabout in Leigh
candidates.evidence_text: Dismay as Leigh veterans' handmade war memorial stolen - BBC News Image source, Reeva Programme Image caption, The soldiers represent members of the armed forces who have died in conflicts since 1914 By Emma Jackson and Richard Stead , North West Published 13 November 2026 Veterans who handmade memorials to fallen soldiers were dismayed to find they had been stolen. They discovered that four of the wooden silhouettes had been taken from the display near Leigh Sports Village in in Greater Manchester was made earlier by members of a group set up to support ex-service people. George Brooks, who launched The Reeva Programme, said: "We are absolutely gutted. "I'm upset, I'm angry, and I'm sad, because I know the effort that went into making every single one of those crosses, making every single one of those tommies." Image source, Reeva Programme Image caption, George Brooks founded The Reeva Programme CIC. The memorial, created on a roundabout, also features 1,228 white crosses to represent local members of the armed forces who were killed in World War Two and subsequent conflicts. George, 35, who served with the Army in Afghanistan, said the stolen figures were important to the community, and to thousands of people they were not just "pieces of wood". Image source, Reeva Programme Image caption, Reeva is named after a therapy dog that helped Brooks cope with PTSD after he left the Army The Reeva Programme provides fully trained assistance dogs to those who have served in the armed forces or emergency services. The theft has been reported to the police, but Brooks posted on social media to say that if whoever had stolen them were to return them, that would be the end of it. candidates.lead: Extra enforcement officers are being recruited ahead of 11-16 year olds being able to ride buses in the city for free from January
candidates.evidence_text: The Mayor of Greater Manchester has said the city region's combined authority is "preparing" for anti-social behaviour ahead of the roll-out of free bus travel for 11 to 16-year-olds From January, the current Our Pass scheme, which gives 16- 18-year-olds free travel on the Bee Network, will be extended to children from the age of 11 Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) confirmed that it was recruiting 20 extra travel safe and enforcement officers to support the 121 existing roles which coincided with the roll-out The city region's Mayor, Bev Craig said the combined authority had been working to make the Bee Network "even safer", and that "we trust our young people." Recent measures included the recent creation of the Transport Policing and Crime Command, which has seen 60 new police officers patrolling Manchester's trams and buses She said the new scheme for 11 to 16-year-olds, expected to benefit 200,000 young people, builds on the Our Pass scheme allowing free bus travel to those aged 16 to 18 which was rolled out in 2019

candidates.lead: John Vickers' victory in the Hindley Green by-election, is being put down to a "Burnham bounce"
candidates.evidence_text: 'Burnham Bounce' sees Labour victory in Wigan by-election - BBC News Image source, LDRS Image caption, John Vickers triumphed in the by-election with 1,201 votes By Chris Gee Local Democracy Reporter Published 13 November 2026 A 'Burnham bounce' has given Labour a big by-election win in the Prime Minister's constituency in Wigan. John Vickers triumphed in the Hindley Green by-election, held following the death of long-standing member Bob Brierley. He topped the polls with 1,201 votes and Reform's Bonnie Clarke was second with 887 votes. It marked the first Wigan borough election won by Labour this year, after they suffered a "wipe-out" in all 25 contested seats for the council in May's local elections. The Hindley Green ward is wholly in the Makerfield parliamentary constituency and the by-election was seen by many as a barometer of support for the new Prime Minister Andy Burnham, with polling happening in his own back yard. In May, Reform won 24 of the 25 seats contested. 'Disillusioned' Now, of the council's 75 seats, Labour have 43 councillors and overall control, Reform still have 25 members, and the remaining seven are independents. Reflecting on the rapid turn in his fortunes, Vickers acknowledged that Burnham's earlier win in Makerfield, on 18 June, "had a lot to do with tonight". He said: "People were disillusioned in May and what happened on June 18 certainly put a lot of faith back in people who had perhaps decided that the Labour Party was not going in the right direction." Outlining his priorities for the ward, he said: "The fact that Hindley Green has no NHS facilities is something we need to put right. "We need to get the pharmacy back to start with and take it from there to get a health centre and associated facilities," he continued. Reflecting on the setback for his party, Wigan Reform leader Paul Watson said there had indeed been a 'Burnham bounce' in the Hindley Green by-election. He said: "We came second tonight but this is a by-election not a local election. "Momentum maybe seems to be with Labour now, after the Burnham bounce, but come May it will be a totally different perspective," adding he was confident Reform would go on to "take control of Wigan Council". A third of seats on the council are set to be contested in local elections in May, 2027. candidates.evidence_text: Work has begun to restore lock gates across Greater Manchester's historical canal network A team has started fitting new handmade gates at Lock 80 on the Rochdale Canal, a waterway opened in 1804 as the first of three trans-Pennine canals, running between Manchester and Sowerby Bridge, West Yorkshire The new gates, at the lock to the east of the city centre in Manchester, were handcrafted from oak in Yorkshire, before being craned into place Each leaf of the upstream gate weighs one-and-a-half tonnes (1,500 kg), and the downstream leaves weigh two-and-a-half tonnes (2,500 kg). They replace gates that were installed at the turn of the millennium It comes after canal gates were replaced in the stretch of canal running through Manchester's Gay Village, in February The Canal and River Trust, the charity that cares for canals and waterways across England and Wales, said the work was one of hundreds of projects over the next five months set to maintain the 2,000-mile canal network

candidates.lead: Work has begun to restore lock gates across Greater Manchester's historical canal network A team has started fitting new handmade gates at Lock 80 on the Rochdale Canal, a waterway opened in 1804 as the first of three trans-Pennine canals, running between Manchester and Sowerby B
candidates.evidence_text: Work has begun to restore lock gates across Greater Manchester's historical canal network A team has started fitting new handmade gates at Lock 80 on the Rochdale Canal, a waterway opened in 1804 as the first of three trans-Pennine canals, running between Manchester and Sowerby Bridge, West Yorkshire The new gates, at the lock to the east of the city centre in Manchester, were handcrafted from oak in Yorkshire, before being craned into place Each leaf of the upstream gate weighs one-and-a-half tonnes (1,500 kg), and the downstream leaves weigh two-and-a-half tonnes (2,500 kg). They replace gates that were installed at the turn of the millennium It comes after canal gates were replaced in the stretch of canal running through Manchester's Gay Village, in February The Canal and River Trust, the charity that cares for canals and waterways across England and Wales, said the work was one of hundreds of projects over the next five months set to maintain the 2,000-mile canal network

candidates.evidence_text: The Christie Hospital 'I remember hearing that word and bursting into tears': Mum's devastating diagnosis after dismissing only symptom Charlotte Moffatt had just one symptom before being given a devastating diagnosis View 2 Images Charlotte Moffatt ( Add to preferred sources Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 07:17, 14 Nov 2026 A Trafford mum has told how she was diagnosed with a form of bowel cancer after initially dismissing her only symptom as a common condition Charlotte Moffatt, 43, from Sale , spotted blood when she wiped after going to the toilet. After searching her symptoms online, she assumed the bleeding was caused by haemorrhoids But after experiencing a particularly heavy bleed, the mum of twins was referred by her GP for further tests Unfortunately, a colonoscopy revealed a large polyp. Subsequent biopsies and scans confirmed the devastating diagnosis of stage three recal cancer Charlotte said: "You just hear the word cancer, everything else goes blank. I just remember hearing that word and bursting into tears, even though I'd kind of prepared myself that that's what they were looking for."

english_fact_card.what_happened: A 'once-in-a-generation' regeneration plan for Old Trafford's Wharfside area is being brought forward by Trafford Council, the Greater Manchester Combined Authority and Manchester United FC. The plan includes new communities, commercial spaces, eateries, hotels, offices and a proposed new 100,000-seat stadium to replace Old Trafford. Residents have raised concerns about matchday parking problems, anti-social behaviour and the use of alleys and front gardens as toilets, which they fear could overshadow the project.

Greater Manchester Police said the arrests follow an investigation into 'drone-flying contraband' being smuggled by air into HMP Forest Bank. The probe was launched earlier this year after In a statement, GMP said: "Today (Friday, November 13), following a knock-on at an address in Swinton, a man and woman in their 60s were arrested on suspicion of conveying articles into prison. They have been taken into custody for questioning "Officers also seized a quantity of class B drugs and cash from the address." Sergeant Jennifer Farrimond, of GMP's Salford Neighbourhood team, said: "This months-long Salford Neighbourhood investigation was launched after staff captured a drone on prison grounds

candidates.evidence_text: Wigan The 'Burnham bounce' strikes again - or was it just a bad night for Reform? “I think people are sick to death of elections” View 4 Images The biggest change since May is new Prime Minister Andy Burnham Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 12:56, 13 Nov 2026 Updated 16:58, 13 Nov 2026 If a week is considered a long time in politics, then six months is an eternity. In May 2026 Labour was hammered in the local elections across Greater Manche The party lost swathes of seats to Reform UK and the Greens in a bruising set of results. It was particularly bad in Wigan , where Reform UK stormed to a massive win and gained 24 of 25 seats up for grabs The results raised questions about whether Labour’s dominance in most of the region’s town halls had come to an end. But a lot has happened since then Of course the biggest change is Andy Burnham swapping the Greater Manchester mayoralty for the Makerfield seat and role of Prime Minister. Last night's council (November 12) by-elections in his Wigan constituency and Oldham (November 12) were seen by some as litmus tests for Labo But looking more closely at the results, the breakdown suggests the story of last night was less a Burnham Bounce and more a Reform slump - or at least a struggle to get their supporters out on the night

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan The 'Burnham bounce' strikes again - or was it just a bad night for Reform? “I think people are sick to death of elections” View 4 Images The biggest change since May is new Prime Minister Andy Burnham Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 12:56, 13 Nov 2026 Updated 16:58, 13 Nov 2026 If a week is considered a long time in politics, then six months is an eternity. In May 2026 Labour was hammered in the local elections across Greater Manche The party lost swathes of seats to Reform UK and the Greens in a bruising set of results. It was particularly bad in Wigan , where Reform UK stormed to a massive win and gained 24 of 25 seats up for grabs The results raised questions about whether Labour’s dominance in most of the region’s town halls had come to an end. But a lot has happened since then Of course the biggest change is Andy Burnham swapping the Greater Manchester mayoralty for the Makerfield seat and role of Prime Minister. Last night's council (November 12) by-elections in his Wigan constituency and Oldham (November 12) were seen by some as litmus tests for Labo But looking more closely at the results, the breakdown suggests the story of last night was less a Burnham Bounce and more a Reform slump - or at least a struggle to get their supporters out on the night

Police are said to be investigating the theft in Leigh, Wigan The wooden, silhouette-style designs were handmade by veterans associated with a social enterprise programme in the area The theft, discovered on Friday morning, comes just 48 hours after Greater Manchester and the nation observed Armistice Day, which marks the day the First World War ended in 1918 The Tommies were installed on the roundabout on Atherleigh Way, near Leigh Sports Village, by social enterprise the Reeva Programme community interest company. candidates.evidence_text: Cheshire The dangerous sexual predator and the victim who spent 20 years trying to put him behind bars Andrew Grierson's offending was first reported more than 20 years ago Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 12:09, 13 A Wigan man has been jailed for historic sex offences committed in Wilmslow over an eight-year period - more than 20 years after it was first reported to the police Andrew Grierson's victim first reported him to police in 2004, over offences which occurred between 1996 and 2004, Cheshire Police said. He was arrested and interviewed, but denied the allegations Concerns had first been raised with Children's Social Care in 1998, the force said, but the matter was closed without police investigation 'due to a lack of evidence' No charges were authorised against him following the first report in 2004, and he was released. The victim then contacted police again in 2011 and provided a 'detailed' account of abuse, but the case was again closed 'following a decision not to seek further CPS advice' The victim contacted Cheshire Police once more in 2021, at which it was finally reopened at her request. The force has admitted that she was 'let down' by police but said that the way it handles reports of sexual offences 'has improved significantly' since the 2000s

After searching her symptoms online, she assumed the bleeding was caused by haemorrhoids But after experiencing a particularly heavy bleed, the mum of twins was referred by her GP for further tests Unfortunately, a colonoscopy revealed a large polyp. Subsequent biopsies and scans confirmed the devastating diagnosis of stage three recal cancer Charlotte said: "You just hear the word cancer, everything else goes blank. english_fact_card.what_happened: A 'once-in-a-generation' regeneration plan for Old Trafford's Wharfside area is being brought forward by Trafford Council, the Greater Manchester Combined Authority and Manchester United FC. The plan includes new communities, commercial spaces, eateries, hotels, offices and a proposed new 100,000-seat stadium to replace Old Trafford. Residents have raised concerns about matchday parking problems, anti-social behaviour and the use of alleys and front gardens as toilets, which they fear could overshadow the project.

candidates.evidence_text: Politics The truth behind the 'Burnham bounce' Greater Manchester saw two council by-elections last night View 4 Images 'Momentum maybe seems to be with Labour now - after the Burnham bounce - but come May it will be a totally different perspective' ( Add to preferred sources Comments News Rob Parsons 18:48, 13 Nov 2026 If a week is considered a long time in politics, then six months is an eternity. In May 2026 Labour - under the leadership of Sir Keir Starmer but with a leadership bid by Andy Burnham looming - were hammered i The party lost swathes of seats to Reform UK and the Greens in a bruising set of results. It was particularly bad in Wigan , where Reform UK stormed to a massive win and gained 24 of 25 seats up for grabs The results in May raised questions about whether Labour’s dominance in most of the region’s town halls had come to an end But a lot has happened since then. Of course the biggest change is Andy Burnham swapping the Greater Manchester mayoralty for the Makerfield seat and role of Prime Minister, elevating him to a global stage View 4 Images Graeme Bandeira's on Burnham's ten-year plan (Image: Graeme Bandeira)

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Brothers among trio jailed after cops uncover plot to fly package into Strangeways using drone Duane Anderson, Jake Anderson, and a third man, Nazar Al-Bakili, have all been locked up Add to preferred sources Comments News Andrew Bardsley Court Two brothers have been jailed after authorities smashed a plot to flood Strangeways prison with contraband by using a drone Duane Anderson, 37, Jake Anderson, 25, and a third man, Nazar Al-Bakili, 35, have all been locked up for their smuggling bid. The plot was uncovered after officers noticed a drone in the sky which appeared to have taken off from a nearby car park, the North West Regional Organise On attendance officers found a Nissan Micra in the car park, with Duane Anderson sat in the driver seat. Al-Bakili ran off and threw a drone controller from his hands The drone was found nearby with a package containing class A and B drugs, mobile phones with accessories and sim cards attached. NWROCU said analysis of Duane Anderson's phone showed that his brother Jake had also been involved. The trio were jailed following a hearing at Manches In a statement, Greater Manchester Police said: "Yesterday (Thursday 12 November) three involved in a drone contraband plot at HMP Manchester have been sentenced after a joint operation with the North West Regional Organised Crime Unit (NWROCU), Greater Manchester Police and HMPP

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham The battle in Oldham few knew was happening One person even said they preferred the paranormal over politics View 3 Images The Rochdale canal in Failsworth (Image: Copyright Unknown) Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 17:55, 13 Nov 2026 A tight contest has been fought in Oldham over the last month – but few people in the area knew it was even happening The Failsworth West by-election on November 12 saw poor turnout , with less than 20 per cent going to the polls and the number of votes cast totalling 1,547. This is less than half the number who turned out to vote earlier this year in the council ward Reform ended the night successfully defending the seat, with Coun Chris Baddeley joining Oldham council’s second largest political group. Labour saw an increase in support compared to May 2026 and doubling their vote share By-elections generally see lower turnout compared to wider elections and this week’s cold weather was thought to be a contributing factor. A sense of disillusionment with politics could have been one, too Out on the streets in and around Failsworth, many were unaware an election had just taken place. Some did not care with a jaded view of politicians, with one person even saying they preferred the paranormal over politics

candidates.evidence_text: Wigan The 'Burnham bounce' strikes again - or was it just a bad night for Reform? “I think people are sick to death of elections” View 4 Images The biggest change since May is new Prime Minister Andy Burnham Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 12:56, 13 Nov 2026 Updated 16:58, 13 Nov 2026 If a week is considered a long time in politics, then six months is an eternity. In May 2026 Labour was hammered in the local elections across Greater Manche The party lost swathes of seats to Reform UK and the Greens in a bruising set of results. It was particularly bad in Wigan , where Reform UK stormed to a massive win and gained 24 of 25 seats up for grabs The results raised questions about whether Labour’s dominance in most of the region’s town halls had come to an end. But a lot has happened since then Of course the biggest change is Andy Burnham swapping the Greater Manchester mayoralty for the Makerfield seat and role of Prime Minister. Last night's council (November 12) by-elections in his Wigan constituency and Oldham (November 12) were seen by some as litmus tests for Labo But looking more closely at the results, the breakdown suggests the story of last night was less a Burnham Bounce and more a Reform slump - or at least a struggle to get their supporters out on the night

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Police want to speak to this man after alleged rape of girl, 15, in Eccles GMP say they are treating the report 'with the utmost seriousness' Add to preferred sources News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 15:12, 13 Nov 2026 View 2 Images The man Greater Manchester Police have appealed to the public for information following reports that a teenage girl was raped in Salford three weeks ago The force said in a release today (November 13) that the incident is believed to have happened between 11pm on October 23 and 2am on October 24 They have now released images of a man they wish to speak to as they believe he could assist with their enquiries. A full investigation is underway with extra patrols in place in the area, the force said The victim, a 15-year-old girl who is being supported by specialist officers, reported that she was approached in the vicinity of Eccles Recreation Ground while out on a walk. The man had then followed her, saying he 'wanted to protect her', the force said "He continued to shout her over and follow her when she attempted to walk away," they said in a statement. "Terrified, the girl stayed with him, reporting that the rape occurred shortly after."

candidates.evidence_text: Cheshire The dangerous sexual predator and the victim who spent 20 years trying to put him behind bars Andrew Grierson's offending was first reported more than 20 years ago Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 12:09, 13 A Wigan man has been jailed for historic sex offences committed in Wilmslow over an eight-year period - more than 20 years after it was first reported to the police Andrew Grierson's victim first reported him to police in 2004, over offences which occurred between 1996 and 2004, Cheshire Police said. He was arrested and interviewed, but denied the allegations Concerns had first been raised with Children's Social Care in 1998, the force said, but the matter was closed without police investigation 'due to a lack of evidence' No charges were authorised against him following the first report in 2004, and he was released. The victim then contacted police again in 2011 and provided a 'detailed' account of abuse, but the case was again closed 'following a decision not to seek further CPS advice' The victim contacted Cheshire Police once more in 2021, at which it was finally reopened at her request. The force has admitted that she was 'let down' by police but said that the way it handles reports of sexual offences 'has improved significantly' since the 2000s

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham The £5m firm and the row over an Oldham mill its owners claim is 'eyesore' There are plans to convert the site into new homes but not everyone is happy about the idea Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter An international firm is in a dispute with its landlord over the use of an Oldham mill its owners claim is an ‘eyesore’. The disagreement came to light after plans for 26 homes were put forward for Wall Hill Mill, off Wall Hill Road in Dobcross The plans would see the buildings demolished. The Saddleworth site sits in the greenbelt, but is classed as previously developed land due to the presence of the mill. There is a large industrial building at the plot, as well as the remains of the older mill Homes in the area have previously been granted planning permission and the land’s owners argue assessments show the land is unviable for employment K&M Global Limited, the firm renting the site, opposes the changes. The company says it is thriving, employs 25 people, has a turnover in excess of £5m a year and invested £300,000 in improving the site The company is a vehicle dismantler, servicer and recycling business. It has been using the site for the last six years. Alan Chorlton , from Chorlton Planning and defending the firm, said it exports to Cyrpus and South Africa

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham The £5m firm and the row over an Oldham mill its owners claim is 'eyesore' There are plans to convert the site into new homes but not everyone is happy about the idea Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter An international firm is in a dispute with its landlord over the use of an Oldham mill its owners claim is an ‘eyesore’. The disagreement came to light after plans for 26 homes were put forward for Wall Hill Mill, off Wall Hill Road in Dobcross The plans would see the buildings demolished. The Saddleworth site sits in the greenbelt, but is classed as previously developed land due to the presence of the mill. There is a large industrial building at the plot, as well as the remains of the older mill Homes in the area have previously been granted planning permission and the land’s owners argue assessments show the land is unviable for employment K&M Global Limited, the firm renting the site, opposes the changes. The company says it is thriving, employs 25 people, has a turnover in excess of £5m a year and invested £300,000 in improving the site The company is a vehicle dismantler, servicer and recycling business. It has been using the site for the last six years. Alan Chorlton , from Chorlton Planning and defending the firm, said it exports to Cyrpus and South Africa

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre Huge new lock gates handcrafted from oak lowered into Rochdale Canal 'These repairs and renewals are critical to keeping canals open' Add to preferred sources Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 06:12, 13 Nov 2026 View 3 Images Huge new handcrafted lock gates are being lifted into place along a stretch of the canal in Manchester city centre . The work, to the east of the city centre on the historic Rochdale Canal, is part of the Canal and River Trust's extensive programme of winter repairs covering 2,00 Earlier this week, a team started fitting new lock gates at Lock 80, near Miles Platting and Victoria Mill. The waterway opened in 1804 as the first of three trans-Pennine canals, running between Manchester and Sowerby Bridge, West Yorkshire The charity, which cares for canals and waterways across England and Wales, said it would be carrying out hundreds of projects over the next five months to maintain the 'living heritage' of the network that was built in the industrial revolution and still functions today Around 136 lock gate leaves – the individual doors or panels – will be replaced under the national programme, as well as repairs to historic locks, bridges, embankments and other infrastructure The new lock gates in Manchester have been handcrafted from oak at the Canal and River Trust's lock gate workshop at Stanley Ferry, Yorkshire, before being craned into place

Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

candidates.evidence_text: Monday 12 October 2026 at 5:22pm Credit: Family photo A police officer called to the home of a mother and her four children murdered hours later in an arson attack told a court she thought their killer was making "empty threats" and did not try to arrest him Pc Gemma Quinn told Bolton Coroner's Court she did not think it necessary to arrest Zak Bolland, 26, "there and then" after a 999 call from Michelle Pearson , 37, when he threatened her son and home on Jackson Street in Walkden , Salford Greater Manchester Police's (GMP) Pc Quinn said she planned to arrest Bolland when she was next on shift in two days' time But after she and a more junior colleague left Ms Pearson's home, Bolland returned less than three hours later to murder her and four of her children in a firebomb attack in the early hours of December 11 2017 The firebombing killed four of Michelle's children, Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three Zak Bolland, 26, and David Worrall, 28, were both jailed for life the following year for the murders

candidates.evidence_text: The Mayor of Greater Manchester, Bev Craig OBE, has called for the city region’s economic growth to put more wealth and opportunity in the hands of local communities, naming co-operatives, social enterprises and community ownership as central to making that happen Craig was speaking at Thrive Together: GM Social Enterprise Summit at New Century Hall, Manchester. The summit was held alongside the National Social Enterprise Summit, ahead of this evening’s (Thursday 12 November) UK Social Enterprise Awards A growing economy does not automatically make life better, Craig said, contrasting Greater Manchester’s visible development with neighbourhoods where residents still struggle financially, and where high streets have lost shops, services and investment The Mayor said: “Good growth is about keeping the benefits of growth in the pockets of the people who create it. Too many of our people still find life too hard. They’ve done the right thing, they’ve got a job, they’ve grafted, and that social contract feels quite broken.” Craig set out a principle: organisations that benefit from public investment should give back through good employment practices, apprenticeships and supply-chain opportunities for local businesses and social enterprises The speech also asked why organisations already delivering for their communities struggle to raise the finance to take on buildings and grow, when commercial developers can get investment

candidates.lead: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026
candidates.evidence_text: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026. The referendum will ask residents whether they want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan to help decide planning applications in the area. The plan sets out local planning policies for Saddleworth and, if approved, will become part of the area’s statutory Development Plan, helping to guide decisions on future planning applications. Residents will be asked the following question: “Do you want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Neighbourhood Plan for Saddleworth to help it decide planning applications in the neighbourhood area?” To vote, residents must be registered to vote in local government elections and have a qualifying address within the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Area. The deadline to register to vote is Tuesday 24 November 2026. Residents who wish to vote by post, proxy or who need a Voter Authority Certificate should also be aware of the following deadlines: - Wednesday 25 November, 5pm: Deadline for new postal vote applications and changes to existing postal voting arrangements. - Wednesday 2 December, 5pm: Deadline for new proxy vote applications and applications for a free Voter Authority Certificate. - Thursday 10 December, 5pm: Deadline for emergency proxy vote applications, where eligible. Residents can read the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan and supporting referendum documents online at: https://www.oldham.gov.uk/info/201235/neighbourhood_planning/2936/saddleworth_neighbourhood_plan Paper copies are also available to view at Lees, Uppermill, Delph and Greenfield libraries, Oldham Council’s reception in Spindles and, by prior arrangement, the Peak District National Park Authority’s office in Bakewell. Following the referendum, the result will be published on Oldham Council’s website. If more than half of those who vote support the plan, it will be adopted as part of the Development Plan for the area and used to help determine planning applications. For further information, residents can contact the council’s Strategic Planning and Information Team on 0161 770 4105 or email spi.consultations@oldham.gov.uk

candidates.title: Could you be Royton North's next councillor? By-election nominations close this Friday
candidates.summary: People are invited to step forward and make a difference in their community
candidates.reason: Dedupe: live item has no exact/history repeat; accepted for editorial selection. | Validator: news item is 9 days old and has no clear new phase for today's digest.

candidates.lead: People are invited to step forward and make a difference in their community
candidates.evidence_text: People are invited to step forward and make a difference in their community. Anyone interested in representing local residents and helping to make decisions affecting the area are invited to consider putting themselves forward as a candidate for the Royton North By-Election. Nominations close at 4pm this Friday (6 November 2026). The by-election has been called following a vacancy in the ward. If there is only one candidate nominated, then that candidate would be elected without contest. If more than one valid nomination is received, residents will go to the polls on Thursday 3 December 2026 to elect their new councillor. This is an opportunity for local people from all backgrounds to represent the interests of their community, raise issues that matter to residents and play a direct role in shaping the future of Royton North and the wider borough. Councillors represent the Council to the community and the community to the Council. Anyone wishing to stand for election can obtain a nomination pack from the Elections Office at the J.R.Clynes Building, Cultural Quarter, Greaves Street, Oldham, OL1 1AL, between 9am and 5pm, or they can be emailed on request by emailing election@oldham.gov.uk. Completed nomination papers must be submitted in person and cannot be accepted by email, post, fax or any other electronic method. Papers can be delivered to the J.R.Clynes Building between 10am and 4pm and no later than 4pm on Friday 6 November. Candidates are advised to book an appointment to submit their papers by contacting the Elections Team at election@oldham.gov.uk. Nomination papers must be delivered to The J.R.Clynes Building. On arrival, candidates will be required to check into reception and then wait to personally deliver them to a member of the elections team. For further information about the by-election or the nomination process, contact the Elections Team at election@oldham.gov.uk

candidates.lead: Primary schools have been recognised for outstanding performance in the 2026 Summer Reading Challenge Read to the Beat
candidates.evidence_text: Primary schools have been recognised for outstanding performance in the 2026 Summer Reading Challenge Read to the Beat. The challenge, delivered by The Reading Agency in partnership with public libraries, encouraged children to discover the joy of reading through the theme Read to the Beat, celebrating music, rhythm and the power of stories. Royton Hall Primary School, St Martin’s Primary School and Greenfield Primary School were recognised as the schools with the highest participation out of 92 schools taking part across Oldham. Representatives from Oldham Libraries and partner Kajima, which supports opportunities to encourage children to read and celebrate their success, visited each school to award book tokens in recognition of pupils’ commitment to reading. Kajima have sponsored the Summer Reading Challenge for the sixth year running, encouraging Oldham children towards a lifelong love of books. The challenge highlights the importance of partnerships between schools, libraries and local organisations in supporting children’s literacy, building reading confidence and making reading an exciting and rewarding experience. Suzanne Hudson, Senior Development Officer for Oldham Heritage, Libraries and Arts said, “It’s fantastic to see so many children across Oldham getting involved in this year’s Summer Reading Challenge. "Reading helps children build confidence, develop their imaginations and discover a lifelong love of books. "We’re delighted to recognise Royton Hall Primary, St Martin’s Primary and Greenfield Primary for their fantastic participation, and we’re incredibly grateful to Kajima for sponsoring the challenge and helping us celebrate the children’s achievements.” Oldham Libraries would also like to thank all participating schools for their support and enthusiasm in helping to make this year’s challenge a success. There’s a warm welcome waiting for you at your local library, with free access to books, fun activities, reading and writing groups and much more to help children to fall in love with reading. Find out more here

candidates.lead: Get ready for a spooky spectacle packed with jaw-dropping performances
candidates.evidence_text: Get ready for a spooky spectacle packed with jaw-dropping performances. Prepare to be wowed in town this Saturday, with an evening packed with entertainment from 5.30pm to 7.30pm. The free event, as part of Oldham's year as the Greater Manchester Town of Culture, will transform Parliament Square into a spook-tacular Halloween and Bonfire Night-inspired celebration with jaw-dropping fiery performances and roaming characters. Visitors can experience the thrills of Juggling Inferno, the spectacular fire and pyrotechnic displays of Helter Skelter Arts, and The Lips Halloween Show. There will also be the chance to come face-to-face with Bessemer the fire-breathing dragon and Toni the giant bat, building towards a breathtaking fireworks display providing a spectacular finale to the celebrations. The stunning show by Helter Skelter Arts features tight choreography and big fire special effects. This mesmerising duo will dance with the flames, creating a display full of emotion and creativity. Juggling Inferno is a beautifully choreographed fire display featuring world class fire entertainers, and the Lips Halloween Show is a big pop-puppetry singalong with something to say. To make it easier for families to enjoy the festivities, there's free parking in all council town centre car parks from 3.30pm. Oldham Council's Director of Communities Neil Consterdine said: "The Feast of Fire is one of the most exciting events in our calendar during Oldham's year as the Greater Manchester Town of Culture — and it's completely free. "We're looking forward to welcoming families or an unforgettable evening of entertainment, and with free parking from 3.30pm, it's the perfect opportunity to come into town, enjoy the Halloween night fun and support our local businesses while you're here." For more information about the Feast of Fire

candidates.evidence_text: From the fabulous Feast of Fire celebrations to the iconic Christmas Lights Switch-On, the town centre will host an exciting calendar of entertainment as the Greater Manchester Town of Culture 2026. The programme will showcase the very best of Oldham's culture, creativity and community spirit with a series of free family-friendly events. The programme begins with the Feast of Fire event on Saturday 31 October 2026. A joint celebration of Halloween and Bonfire Night, this spellbinding event will light up the heart of the town centre with fire dance performances and The Lips Halloween Show by Puppets with Guts followed by a pyrotechnic Halloween fireworks display in the area around Parliament Square from 5.30pm. Then, just two weeks later, the festive season will officially begin with the Oldham Christmas Lights Switch-On event on Saturday 14 November, starting from 1pm. The day will feature meet and greets with Peppa Pig, appearances from Oldham's mascots and activities by the Spindles Kids Club. The celebrations will continue into the evening with the big Switch On Show from 5.30pm featuring Father Christmas, Peppa Pig's Dance Party, Oldham Rock Choir and performances from Fierce Dance. The Mayor of Oldham Cllr Pam Byrne will also take part in the celebrations before a local school child competition winner will switch on the town's Christmas lights. The evening will conclude with a festive fireworks finale, accompanied by a lights and laser show. To coincide with the switch on, the Festive Fun with Peppa Cinema Experience is coming to the Odeon at Parliament Square on Saturday 14 and Sunday 15 November, at 10am and 11.30am both days. Join Peppa Pig and her family at the cinema for a festive big-screen experience as they celebrate Evie’s first Christmas. To book click here. The following weekend, on Saturday 12 December, the town centre will be transformed for Winter Wonderland Saturday. candidates.lead: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović .
candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . Stockport is kicking off Christmas in suitably weird and wonderful fashion, as Spectacular Sunday returns for its fourth year on Sunday 15 November More than 200 performers and 50 free shows will take over the town centre, transforming streets and squares into stages for giant puppets, circus acts, live music, comedy and all manner of festive surprises Among the highlights is the enormous Snow Lion, joined by dancing elves and towering stiltwalkers. There’s also Over The Moon, a circus adventure with an intergalactic twist, and Hydropunk, an interactive spectacle involving water-powered pipes, pumps, sprays and puzzles And if you fancy a rave between the Christmas shopping, The Miniscule of Sound, officially the world’s smallest nightclub, is back for another year. Expect big tunes in a very, very small space

evidence_texts: Credit: Ben Houdijk via Shutterstock AO Arena Victoria Station Approach, Hunts Bank, Manchester M3 1AR 21 November 2026 If you’re planning ahead for the biggest live nights in the city, Fontaines D.C. are embarking on a 20-arena European and UK tour this autumn, including a Manchester date at the AO Arena on 21 November. Ahead of their massive Heaton Park take over next summer, the Dublin boys are set to give fans a first listen to their spectacular new album ‘ Dopamine Chamber ‘ live on stage. After huge success with 2024 album ‘ Romance ‘, Fontaines D.C. have been catapulted into the limelight, with songs like Favourite, Starburster and It’s Amazing to be Young on the top of playlists the world over – and no doubt Grian and the boys will be happy to revisit those hits. candidates.lead: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre […] The post Sona Jobarteh Tour appeared first on Band on the Wall
candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. Born in London into a Gambian griot lineage of seven centuries, she began learning the kora at age three with her brother Tunde Jegede and father Sanjally Jobarteh; her cousin was the late Toumani Diabaté. She studied at the Royal College of Music, the Purcell School of Music and SOAS University of London. In 2015 she founded The Gambia Academy, which puts African history and culture at the centre of its curriculum, and she has keynoted forums hosted by the UN and the World Trade Organization. In 2023 Berklee College of Music awarded her an honorary Doctorate in Music alongside Usher and Roberta Flack

candidates.lead: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians.
candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

candidates.evidence_text: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! Across this 5 day course, we’ll be exploring music for film, and working on composing music for the silent film ‘A Trip to the Moon’. The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. You can bring your own instruments, but we have keyboards, guitars, bass, violins, drums and percussion on site which can be used if you don’t have an instrument. Please email learning@bandonthewall.org if you have any questions about this course

candidates.evidence_text: The Olllam is a band that fuses Irish traditional music with the modern jazz/post-rock energy of Detroit. Led by uilleann piper John McSherry, the band features Joe Dart (Vulfpeck), Michael Shimmin, Ross Ainslie, Seán O’Meara, and Joe Hettinga. Following their acclaimed album elllegy (RTÉ Radio 1 Best Group), The Olllam has collaborated with GRAMMY-nominated producer Zedd, shared the stage in Belfast with actor Anthony Boyle (Netflix’s House of Guinness), and recently completed a landmark U.S. tour in November 2025. From ancient airs to future soundscapes, The Olllam is not just carrying the tradition forward—they’re reinventing it

A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

It is Open Restaurant Group’s ninth restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Didsbury in Sep At the focus of the restaurant is a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, which places guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. The interiors feature four-metre elm trees, curved booth seating and a brass wine display, so the atmosphere and experienc Award-winning Andrew Sheridan brings his internationally inspired approach to Counter, building on a career that has seen multiple restaurants under his direction feature in the prestigious Michelin Guide. Loungers, the West Country‑based café‑bar group, will open Fosforo Lounge, King Street in Stretford on Saturday 28th November 2026, creating around 30 new jobs for local people.. . Fosforo Lounge will be open all day, every day, serving breakfast, brunch, lunch, dinner and drinks, with dedicated kids’, gluten‑free and vegan menus. . The site on King Street has been transformed by the Loungers design team into a warm, eclectic ‘home from home’ – their signature style. Fosforo translates to matchstick and is a nod to Manchester-based painter LS Lowry’s ‘matchstick men’ style.. . Fosforo Lounge’s all‑day menu will cater for every taste, from hearty comfort food to healthier choices and indulgent treats. Families are a major focus, with games, books, colouring materials, high chairs and baby‑changing facilities available for Little Loungers.. . With community at its heart, Fosforo Lounge will offer a welcoming space for regular meet‑ups, business catch‑ups, book clubs, knitting groups, parent‑and‑baby sessions, creative workshops and more. Local groups looking for a friendly, flexible venue will be encouraged to get in touch.. . Vix Connolly, General Manager, Fosforo Lounge said: “We’re so looking forward to welcoming everyone to Fosforo Lounge on the 28th November. candidates.lead: Posted by Manchester Digital Introducing The Inside Track: A new way to get more from your Manchester Digital membership
candidates.evidence_text: Stay connected. Know what's next. We're launching The Inside Track , a new monthly online session designed to help Manchester Digital members stay informed, discover new opportunities and make the most of their membership Whether you've recently joined Manchester Digital or have been part of our community for years, The Inside Track is your chance to catch up with our team, find out what's happening across the network and explore ways to get more involved Taking place on the last Wednesday of each month, these free, members-only sessions will bring you up to speed on the latest developments, events and opportunities across Manchester Digital, all in just 30 minutes Each session will feature a topical focus, alongside practical updates on upcoming events, programmes, speaking opportunities and ways to raise your business's profile There'll also be time to ask questions, share your priorities and find out how we can help you get more value from your membership Our first edition at midday on 25th November will focus on some of the biggest opportunities coming up across the Manchester Digital community

candidates.lead: Posted by Manchester Digital Manchester Digital Festival 2027: Programme revealed as tickets go on sale
candidates.evidence_text: Five days. Five themes. One city shaping its digital future. The first Manchester Digital Festival takes place from 8–12 February 2027 with its biggest and boldest programme yet. Manchester Digital has unveiled the programme for Manchester Digital Festival 2027 (MDF27 ) , bringin Taking place from Monday 8 to Friday 12 February 2027 , the festival marks an exciting new chapter for Manchester Digital, building on the success of Digital Skills Festival and expanding its scope to celebrate the full breadth of Greater Manchester's digital and technology secto The launch also comes as Manchester Digital celebrates its 25th anniversary , providing an opportunity to reflect on the people, businesses and innovations that have shaped the region's tech ecosystem, while looking ahead to what comes next With 15 events already announced and more to come, the first wave of the MDF27 programme offers everything from industry conferences and leadership discussions to careers events, founder stories and opportunities to explore emerging technologies Tickets for most events are now available , with further announcements expected in the coming months Under the banner Building our digital tomorrow , MDF27 introduces a new five-day format, with each day dedicated to a different theme reflecting the opportunities and challenges facing Greater Manchester's digital and technology sector

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The city’s favourite alpine pop-up brings another round of festive magic back to Great Northern Square, as Bar Hütte celebrates ten years of après-ski fun Once again transforming the Deansgate plaza into a twinkling mountain resort, Bar Hütte stages another winter wonderland packed with cosy karaoke cabins, a heated party lodge and live music throughout the colder months Inspired by Europe’s best ski destinations, the pop-up offers ultimate festive escapism, from winter cocktails and steaming pizzas to private karaoke and Christmas party packages. Four-legged family members can also join the fun with the return of Bark Hütte, a pup-sized hütte wi Alongside karaoke, the pop-up’s popular wreath-making workshops will return. Priced at £55 per person, including a glass of fizz or mulled wine, classes will be running on Sun 29 Nov (2pm-4pm) and Tue 1 Dec (6.30pm) Perfect for families, Bae Huttë’s Santa Claus Club is back, too. Enjoy an hour of karaoke with a free hot chocolate per child (up to six children) and colouring pads for the kids. Plus, there’ll be an opportunity to grab a selfie with Father Christmas himself on Sun 13 Dec and Su Booking is strongly advised, but walk-ins are also welcome. There will also be plenty of outdoor seating available under a heated stretched tent, giving Christmas partygoers the chance to get merry without getting cold

candidates.evidence_text: A special evening celebrating one of Manchester’s most influential musicians, Vini Reilly and his post-punk project The Durutti Column, comes to Albert Hall this month Fresh from sold-out Southbank Centre performances, a unique ensemble will reinterpret key works from The Durutti Column’s remarkable six-decade career in Reilly’s home city on Thu 19 Nov Presenting the one-night-only For Vini show is producer Keir Stewart, who has worked with Reilly and drummer Bruce Mitchell since 1998’s Time Was Gigantic… When We Were Kids album For the performance, Stewart (guitar, bass, samples, keys) is joined by The Durutti Column collaborators Sam Morris (French horn), Caoilfhionn Rose (vocals and piano) and Liz Rossi (violin and piano) Audiences can expect to hear material that spans releases on Factory Records through to tracks from Renascent , creating a rare and immersive live experience that honours one of Manchester’s most singular musical voices, one recently cited as a key influence on Harry Styles’ late Coinciding with the homecoming show at Albert Hall, The Durutti Column have joined with Four Tet for an official remix of Your Shadow at Morning. Find out with Jonathan Schofield Tours, with whom you’ll track Ancoats’ changes by strolling its streets, crossing its canals, and taking a look inside one of its most fascinating buildings Starting at Cutting Room Square, your expert tour guide will reveal the layers of history that make Ancoats special, from its place in establishing Manchester’s reputation as ‘Cottonopolis’ to the notorious street gangs, or ‘scuttlers’, who once patrolled and fought here But this winsome stroll is also about the urban regeneration and cultural energy of Ancoats today, which boasts everything from grassroots theatres to Manchester’s only Michelin-starred restaurant

This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. candidates.evidence_text: Manchester United FC Old Trafford's 'once-in-a-generation' plan that could be ruined by 'weeing in the garden' Residents want to see a solution to matchday parking problems, related anti-social behaviour and the use of alleys and front gardens as an a A ‘once-in-a-generation' regeneration opportunity is being brought forward in Old Trafford - but it risks being overshadowed by matchday anti-social behaviour, neighbours fear Trafford council , the Greater Manchester Combined Authority and Manchester United FC are teaming up on an ambitious project that could see a forgotten part of the borough transformed beyond recognition. Bosses want to see ‘thriving’ new communities built in the Wharfside area, w Commercial spaces, eateries, hotels and offices are also in the line-up . And at the heart of the development – and the catalyst for it – is a proposed new stadium to replace the Theatre of Dreams With 100,000 seats, Man U’s promised new home ground is expected to be the largest in the UK. The Wharfside scheme is likely to take decades to deliver in full But the results of a consultation on a plan suggest that, for some residents in the area, their priorities are more immediate and their ambitions for the area somewhat less lofty

После выхода хита «Kasaba» в 2008 году Мурат Далкылыч стал одной из главных фигур турецкой поп-музыки. Он известен своим узнаваемым голосом, энергичными выступлениями и популярными песнями, среди которых «Bir Güzellik Yap». За годы карьеры в музыке, написании песен и кино он приобрел большую и преданную аудиторию как в Турции, так и за ее пределами. 29 января 2027 года Мурат Далкылыч выступит в indigo at The O2 в Лондоне. Вас ждет яркий вечер турецкой поп-музыки, живого исполнения и любимых хитов. Не упустите возможность увидеть Мурата Далкылыча вживую в Лондоне! Предварительный заказ
